scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): backs strong wilderness laws while arguing that protecting every remaining area is too rigid; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Wild places, once destroyed, can almost never be recovered.
Some people claim that nations should pass laws to preserve any remaining wilderness areas in their natural state.
I strongly support protecting wilderness, but I believe a law covering every remaining area would be too rigid.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why preserving wilderness is vital

sentences.text: First, protecting wilderness through law brings deep and lasting benefits.
Wild areas shelter rare species and keep the natural systems we all depend on in balance.
For example, protected forests clean our air and water and guard plants found nowhere else.
This shows that preserving wilderness protects human life as well as nature.
Natural places also give people beauty, peace, and a sense of wonder.
Strong laws are often the only thing standing between wild land and its destruction.
To this extent, laws to protect wilderness are clearly wise.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why 'any remaining' is too rigid

sentences.text: Second, however, a law protecting every remaining wild area would be too rigid to be fair.
Some communities sit on land that must be used to meet urgent human needs.
Consider a poor region that needs a small part of its wild land for water, food, or shelter.
Such cases show that an absolute law could trap people in poverty for the sake of untouched land.
Wisely chosen limits can protect most wilderness while leaving room for genuine human needs.
A rigid rule covering every area would ignore the real differences between places and situations.
Protection, then, should be strong but flexible rather than absolute.
In conclusion, nations should pass strong laws to protect their wilderness areas.
But a rule preserving every remaining area without exception would be too rigid and unfair.
The wisest laws protect most wilderness while allowing for the most pressing human needs.
